title: bug: the normal approval path records a plan.approve risk fact, so automatic preview reaches RISK_TIER_UNCLASSIFIABLE on the real product journey
description:
Found by an external review and re-measured by architect-bb193f43 at main 0c215e82 on 2026-09-11.

THE GAP. Automatic preview asks the policy for a risk fact bound to the `preview.decide` action. The production risk writer records one bound to `plan.approve`.

MEASURED, in `apps/daemon/src/planning/policy-risk-leg.ts`:

    /** One domain action shared by both approval transports and the policy.validate consumer. */
    export const POLICY_RISK_APPROVAL_ACTION = "plan.approve" as const;
    ...
    actionKind: POLICY_RISK_APPROVAL_ACTION,

That constant is the ONLY action the normal journey writes. Nothing on the ordinary path writes a `preview.decide` risk fact, so when automatic preview looks one up it finds nothing and the reproduced result is `RISK_TIER_UNCLASSIFIABLE`.

WHY THE SUITE IS GREEN ANYWAY. The unattended tests INSERT the missing preview-specific record by hand as fixture setup. The gate is therefore proven against a world the product never produces. This is the shape epic rail 4 exists to catch: the machinery exists, its production path does not close.

WHAT THIS ROW OWES. Make the ordinary product journey supply what the automatic preview gate requires - or make the gate consume what the journey actually records. Either direction is acceptable; what is not acceptable is leaving the hand-inserted fixture as the only way the gate ever sees its input. Decide it from the contracts and say which you chose and why.

DEPENDS ON task-3ccb12a92f69432bb6996a3a4348e573 (the effective-policy selector). That row rewrites which slice governs the same gate; landing these concurrently would put two rows in `preview-auto-composition.ts` at once. Read its completionSummary before planning.

VERIFY BEFORE PLANNING: `grep -rn 'preview.decide' apps/daemon/src --include=*.ts | grep -v test` to see who asks for the fact, and `grep -rn 'POLICY_RISK_APPROVAL_ACTION' apps/daemon/src` to see who writes it. Do not plan against the excerpt above.
definitionOfDone: An end-to-end arm drives the ORDINARY journey through production handlers only - no hand-inserted risk record anywhere in the arm - and reaches an automatic preview decision. Assert the decision, and assert the arm contains no fixture write of a preview risk fact.

A negative arm asserts that when the risk fact is genuinely absent or unclassifiable, the gate still refuses with `RISK_TIER_UNCLASSIFIABLE` and its layer. Fixing the happy path must not remove the fail-closed answer.

Every existing unattended test that hand-inserts the preview-specific record is either deleted or rewritten to use the production path. Grep for the fixture insert and show zero remaining, or name each survivor and why it must stay.
Non-vacuity: remove the production write introduced by this row and confirm the end-to-end arm goes red with `RISK_TIER_UNCLASSIFIABLE`. Quote the red.

1. CAN A STALE OR REPLAYED RUN EVALUATION PUBLISH DAEMON_VERIFIED FOR A GOAL IT DOES NOT BELONG TO? No, and there are four independent fences, three of which existed and one of which I added. The runId is never caller-supplied: it comes from `goal.graph.planningRunRef`, and `readCriterionGoal:22-23` refuses unless EXACTLY ONE active compiled graph carries this `goalRef`. `readRunPolicyEvaluation` addresses the run's own aggregate, refuses AMBIGUOUS on two rows, and refuses RUN_MISMATCH on a row that STATES another run. My graph pin then requires the evaluation's EXACT SINGLE `graphNodeRevisionRefs` member to equal `goal.binding.graphContentHash`, which `readCriterionGoal:29-31` has itself already cross-checked against the encoded graph, the sealed authority's revision and `bound.binding.goalRef`. A stale revision's row therefore fails the digest; a foreign run's row fails uniqueness or linkage. Arms 8 and the two pin arms cover both.

2. DOES ANY ABSENCE PATH PRODUCE A NULL TIER WITHOUT truthClass UNKNOWN? No. `withheld()` is the ONE constructor for every refusal and hard-codes both halves; the single DAEMON_VERIFIED return is unreachable unless `riskTier !== null`. Mutant E (publish a withheld fact as DAEMON_VERIFIED) reds 9 of 13 arms, so the property is pinned rather than asserted.
